maya: Heads-up: runtime flipped defaults -> batching now 'aggressive' and added a new quant profile. We need a short relnote, migration steps, and to update the py/js snippets. tagging @rachel @samir
rachel: On it. Can someone give me the user-facing bullets so I can write a concise 2-line relnote + snippet examples?
samir: Bullets from runtime: 1) default `batching.policy` = "aggressive" (improves throughput for long sequences) 2) new quant profile `q8-dynmix` available on x86-gpu images 3) q4_0/q4_1 remain supported but are marked deprecated in console
kevin: Callout: small/short-sequence latency may increase ~10-25ms in low-concurrency single-worker setups. We should include a Known Issue and opt-out instructions.
maya: Snippet sweep: update py sample that used `batching=None` and the JS quickstart that referenced `quant_profile` names. Also add a migration section with Console + CLI steps.
rachel: Draft relnote copy: "Serving defaults updated: batching set to 'aggressive' to improve throughput for long-sequence workloads. New quant profile `q8-dynmix` available; legacy q4_* profiles are deprecated. Known issue: sub-100-token latency can regress in some low-concurrency environments; see migration notes to opt out."
samir: Migration snippets: per-call opt-out and global override. Python example for per-call opt-out:
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-1-small", prompt=prompt, config={"batching": {"policy": "none"}, "quant_profile": "q4_1"})
```
CLI example for private deploys / global override:
```bash
redwoodctl set global-config --batching.policy=none --quant_profile=q4_1
redwoodctl config get global  # verify
```
kevin: QA note: run perf test with realistic sequence-length mix before changing defaults. For Dedicated customers, stage canary with 20% prod-like traffic, monitor p50/p95 for <100-token requests.
